title: Infrastructure patterns for agentic applications
excerpt: AI agents are long-running, stateful, and non-deterministic. Learn the queue, workflow, and reliability patterns that take agents from demo to production.
content_html:
Most teams start building agents the same way they build any other web feature: wrap the model in a route handler, parse the request, and wait for the response.

This is fine for a demo. It's also the first thing to break in production.

Agents are long-running, stateful, and non-deterministic. They call tools, wait for external APIs, branch into subtasks, hit rate limits, and crash halfway through multi-step sequences. If your agent is tied to a single HTTP request, you've coupled your application's reliability to the wall-clock time of a non-deterministic loop.

Moving past the demo means breaking that coupling. This post walks through the three core patterns teams use to turn fragile agent scripts into scalable, resilient production systems.

At the core of an agent is a loop: receive a goal, decide what to do next, call a model or tool, observe the result, update state, repeat until done. That loop has a few properties that make it hostile to naive web architectures.

Agents are long-running. A normal API request should finish quickly. Agents often don't, sometimes taking hours or even days to complete.

Agents are stateful. A run isn't one function call. It's a goal, a plan, tool calls and outputs, retries, errors, decisions, and a final output. If the process crashes, you need to know what already happened. If not, you either lose progress or rerun work blindly. Neither is great, especially for long-running agents.

The model chooses the next action at runtime, which makes recovery, replay, and debugging much harder.

A run may take three steps or thirty. It may fan out across several tools, wait for a human, produce large intermediate artifacts, or stop early. Infrastructure has to set boundaries around that unpredictability with timeouts, budgets, checkpoints, approvals, and explicit termination conditions.

Taken together, these properties mean agents need more than model calls wrapped in application code. They need architecture that decouples runs from requests, and infrastructure that preserves progress, records decisions, controls side effects, and manages artifacts separately from model context.

The first production pattern is to stop running the whole agent inside the web request. A request is the wrong lifetime for an agent run. It should create a durable run record, enqueue the work, and return immediately.

That gives the application a simple boundary:

The API enqueues the job. The queue stores the job durably. The worker executes the job. The database records progress.

The client gets a run ID immediately. The agent runs somewhere else. The user checks status, subscribes to updates, or receives a callback when the run completes.

A queue is a durable buffer between the thing that creates work and the thing that performs it. This is the default starting point when runs are longer than a normal request, tasks are mostly independent, and you need worker scaling, retries, or burst absorption.

The trap: a queue knows a job exists, but it doesn't know the logical process that job belongs to. One background job is fine. Twenty dependent steps, three retries, two branches, and a human approval pause is not something a queue manages for you. You'll build that logic yourself. As we'll see later, that's where workflow engines come in.

Reliability: safe retries and partial failure

Moving work to a queue solves the lifetime problem. It does not solve for durability of execution.

Most production queues are at-least-once: a job may run more than once. That's a deliberate tradeoff to avoid losing work, and your code has to survive it. Once an agent can call tools, write records, send messages, or provisions resources, retry behavior becomes part of the application’s correctness model.

Two disciplines matter most. Idempotency answers what happens when a single step runs twice. Compensation answers what happens when a run stops partway through a sequence of steps. Retries make the first a requirement. Permanent failures make the second necessary for production. Agents that touch remote services needs both.

Bad worker code assumes no crash between steps:

Better code creates an idempotency boundary:

For agents, every side-effecting tool call needs the same treatment: check for a completed record before calling the tool, upsert a "running" record, call the tool, mark it complete.

Retry is not a recovery strategy unless the retried operation is safe.

Consider an agent that completes three of five steps:

  1. it charges a card,
  2. provisions a resource,
  3. and sends a confirmation email.

Then step four then fails permanently. None of the first three steps can be rolled back with a database transaction, since a charge is not undone by deleting a database row; the money has already moved. Restarting the run from step one would recharge the card and resend the email, recreating the exact duplicate-side-effect problem idempotency was meant to prevent.

Distributed systems have a standard answer to this: the saga pattern. For every side-effecting action an agent can take, define a compensating action that reverses the effect. A charge is reversed with a refund. An email is reversed with a correction message. When a run fails permanently, the orchestrator walks the completed steps in reverse order and runs their compensations.

Compensations must be idempotent in the same way forward actions are. Compensations can also fail on their own; a refund API can be unavailable just as easily as a charge API. A compensation chain needs a bounded retry, a dead-letter path for compensations that will not complete, and a manual escape hatch. Without these, a failed run can end up half-undone instead of half-done, which is not an improvement.

Compensation is not always the right response to a partial failure. If four of five parallel sub-orders succeeded and one failed, completing the four and dropping the fifth is often the better outcome. This avoids unwinding work that succeeded. Compensation is worth building when partial success is unacceptable, not as a default response to any failure.

Idempotency covers a step that runs twice. Compensation covers a run that stops halfway through. Both are required whether the run is executed by a simple worker or by a workflow engine.

A queue distributes work, but it does not remember the shape of a run. It knows that a job exists. It does not know that step three depends on step two, that a human approval is pending, that two branches need to join before synthesis, or that compensation should run if the final step fails.

Once the hard part is no longer where should this job run? but what should happen next, given what already happened?, you have moved from queueing into orchestration.

A workflow engine provides that orchestration layer. It stores the history of a run: which steps started, completed, failed, retried, timed out, or waited for external input. In a workflow, a crash doesn't mean starting over.

Every workflow system divides the code into the same two roles: a coordinator that decides what happens next, and steps that do the actual work — model calls, tool executions, record writes. The names vary from engine to engine, but the division of responsibility is the concept that matters: decisions live in one layer, effects live in the other.

The coordinator has one hard rule: given the same history, it must always make the same decisions. This is because of how recovery works. After a crash, the engine rebuilds a run by re-executing the decision logic from the top, substituting recorded results for work that already completed. Replay only lands in the same place if the code decides the same way every time. So anything that could answer differently on a second pass — a model call, the current time, a random number, a call to an external service — belongs in a step, where the result is recorded the first time it runs and read back from history ever after. A stray clock read inside the coordinator, and a resumed run silently diverges from its own history. Durable execution tells you where a run was when it crashed. It does not remove the need for idempotency, because steps can still run more than once. This is why a workflow engine is the natural home for compensation logic: it already tracks which steps completed, which is the record a saga needs to walk backward.

Scaling workflows: fan-out, fan-in, and contention

Workflows become especially useful when a run branches. Fan-out is the common shape: a lead agent breaks a goal into independent subtasks, sends each to a worker or subagent, and then synthesizes the results.

This buys parallelism and fresh context windows, which is useful for research, document analysis, and other breadth-first work. But the hard part is not dispatching the workers. It is coordinating the fan-in: what happens if one branch fails, how many failures are tolerable, whether to synthesize partial results, and how to avoid waiting forever. A queue can run the workers. A workflow decides what happens next.

Fan-out is worth using when subtasks are independent, mostly read-only, and parallelizable. It works poorly when subtasks are tightly coupled or need to share state that keeps changing. Adding agents also adds cost and coordination overhead, so the question of how many agents to use matters more than the mechanics of spawning them.

Fan-out also introduces contention. A system can work with three parallel subagents and fail at eleven, even when there is plenty of aggregate provider capacity. Uncoordinated calls can collide on the same rate limit, exhaust the same connection pool, or retry at the same time. Treat providers, databases, and model APIs as shared resources: cap concurrency, use token buckets where needed, and back off when the shared resource pushes back.

At scale, a workflow coordinates the process and a queue distributes execution. They are not competitors; they operate at different layers.

Two details carry the weight here. Promise.allSettled keeps one failed branch from poisoning the entire fan-in, and the success threshold makes the partial-failure policy explicit: the workflow, not the queue, decides whether the run can proceed with what came back.

This is the mature pattern for high-scale agentic systems: durable process state, multiple worker pools, rate-limited dispatch, audibility. The cost is real operational complexity. You now have an API plane, an orchestration plane, and an execution plane. This is worth it when the workload demands it.

The patterns above are platform-agnostic. You can assemble them from any queue, any workflow engine, and any worker fleet. The question is how much of that assembly you want to own and operate.

On Render, the answer is almost none of it. Your web service is the API; Render Workflows is everything else. You define tasks as plain TypeScript or Python functions, and the platform provides the queue, the workers, the retries, the isolation, and per-run observability. There is no queue to provision, no worker fleet to keep warm, and no orchestrator cluster to operate.

Take a concrete agent: given a goal like “summarize how our top three competitors price their enterprise tiers,” it plans, searches, reads, and synthesizes a brief. Written as workflow code, it is exactly the loop from the start of this post — a coordinator that decides, and steps that act:

Three things to notice:

This is the entire execution plane. There is no queue client, no message schema, no polling loop, no worker registration. Three task() wrappers replace the API → Queue → Worker plumbing from the first pattern. When runAgent calls decide(...) or executeAction(...), that is not a local function call — because the functions are wrapped in task(), each call starts a chained task run on its own on-demand instance, with its own retry policy and its own compute profile. Promise.all is the fan-out; the platform handles dispatch, isolation, and retry.

The loop is the agent. The coordinator doesn’t execute a fixed plan. Each pass through the loop decides again, given everything that has already happened — so actions can run in sequence across iterations, in parallel within one, and the run terminates when the model decides it is done (bounded by the task’s timeout).

One agent run is one tree of task runs. The run of runAgent is the root; every decide and executeAction run chains off it. Render tracks the whole tree — status, retries, logs per run — so “what did the agent do?” is a question the dashboard can answer. If your application needs its own record, store the root run’s ID and go from there.

Starting an agent run, from your web service or anywhere else, is one SDK call:

startTask is the enqueue. The platform stores the work durably, dispatches it, and exposes its status — the entire boundary from the first pattern, in one call. (If the caller wants to block until completion, runTask does that instead; for an API request boundary, startTask is the right fit.)

Workflows is the center of gravity, but the rest of the platform composes in when a run needs more. A Cron Job calling startTask gives you scheduled agents. Key Value gives you token buckets when parallel runs contend on a shared rate limit. Postgres holds large artifacts, so tasks pass IDs instead of payloads — state that must outlive a run goes in a store; state that must not leak between runs dies with the container. None of this is required to get started; each is one primitive, added when the workload demands it.

Workflows removes queue and worker plumbing. Today, it does not remove application-level correctness work: idempotency, compensation, artifact storage, trace propagation, approval boundaries, cost controls, and rate limits are still yours to build with the patterns in this post.

That boundary is moving, though. Much of this list is exactly where Workflows is headed: stronger durability guarantees, first-class idempotency, and human-in-the-loop primitives like native approval gates are all on the roadmap. The patterns in this post will stay the same, but expect more of them to ship as platform features instead of application code you maintain.

Workflows are now in Beta, with current limitations around supported languages, scheduling, Blueprint support, and HIPAA-compatible hosts.

What no platform can remove is the design burden of orchestration. You still have to decide where state lives, where retries are safe, where approval happens, and how a run is traced end to end. The platform's job is to make those decisions cheap to implement, not to make them for you.

The next generation of agentic applications will be built like distributed systems, whether the underlying infrastructure is hand-rolled or managed.

Remember that a queue asks: where should this work run? A workflow asks: what should happen next, given what has already happened? An agent asks: what should I do next to accomplish the goal?

Render Workflows can make the execution layer simpler. It can start task runs, queue them, retry them, and show their status. But the application still owns the semantics of the run: what counts as progress, which side effects are safe to retry, where artifacts live, when a human must approve, and how partial failure is repaired.

That is the real boundary. Infrastructure moves work. Workflows preserve progress. Agents choose actions. Reliable agentic applications come from keeping those responsibilities separate, even when the platform makes them easy to deploy together.

sentences.zh: 代理通常不会这样做，有时需要数小时甚至数天才能完成。

blocks.html_en: Agents are stateful. A run isn't one function call. It's a goal, a plan, tool calls and outputs, retries, errors, decisions, and a final output. If the process crashes, you need to know what already happened. If not, you either lose progress or rerun work blindly. Neither is great, especially for long-running agents.

sentences.en: Agents are stateful.
sentences.zh: 代理是有状态的。

sentences.en: A run isn't one function call.
sentences.zh: 一次运行不是一次函数调用。

sentences.en: It's a goal, a plan, tool calls and outputs, retries, errors, decisions, and a final output.
sentences.zh: 它是一个目标、一个计划、工具调用和输出、重试、错误、决策和最终输出。

sentences.en: If the process crashes, you need to know what already happened.
sentences.zh: 如果进程崩溃，您需要知道已经发生了什么。

sentences.en: If not, you either lose progress or rerun work blindly.
sentences.zh: 如果没有，您要么会失去进度，要么盲目地重新运行工作。

sentences.en: Neither is great, especially for long-running agents.
sentences.zh: 两者都不是很好，特别是对于长期运行的代理来说。

blocks.html_en: Agents are non-deterministic. Traditional workflow code says:

sentences.en: Agents are non-deterministic.
sentences.zh: 代理是不确定的。

sentences.en: Traditional workflow code says:
sentences.zh: 传统的工作流程代码是这样的：

blocks.html_en: Agent code says:

sentences.en: Agent code says:
sentences.zh: 代理代码说：

blocks.html_en: The model chooses the next action at runtime, which makes recovery, replay, and debugging much harder.

sentences.en: The model chooses the next action at runtime, which makes recovery, replay, and debugging much harder.
sentences.zh: 该模型在运行时选择下一个操作，这使得恢复、重放和调试变得更加困难。

blocks.html_en: A run may take three steps or thirty. It may fan out across several tools, wait for a human, produce large intermediate artifacts, or stop early. Infrastructure has to set boundaries around that unpredictability with timeouts, budgets, checkpoints, approvals, and explicit termination conditions.

sentences.en: A run may take three steps or thirty.
sentences.zh: 跑步可能需要三步或三十步。

sentences.en: It may fan out across several tools, wait for a human, produce large intermediate artifacts, or stop early.
sentences.zh: 它可能会分散到多个工具上，等待人类，产生大量的中间工件，或者提前停止。

sentences.en: Infrastructure has to set boundaries around that unpredictability with timeouts, budgets, checkpoints, approvals, and explicit termination conditions.
sentences.zh: 基础设施必须通过超时、预算、检查点、批准和明确的终止条件来围绕这种不可预测性设置边界。

blocks.html_en: Taken together, these properties mean agents need more than model calls wrapped in application code. They need architecture that decouples runs from requests, and infrastructure that preserves progress, records decisions, controls side effects, and manages artifacts separately from model context.

sentences.en: Taken together, these properties mean agents need more than model calls wrapped in application code.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，这些属性意味着代理需要的不仅仅是包装在应用程序代码中的模型调用。

sentences.en: They need architecture that decouples runs from requests, and infrastructure that preserves progress, records decisions, controls side effects, and manages artifacts separately from model context.
sentences.zh: 他们需要将运行与请求分离的架构，以及保留进度、记录决策、控制副作用以及与模型上下文分开管理工件的基础设施。

blocks.html_en: The first production pattern is to stop running the whole agent inside the web request. A request is the wrong lifetime for an agent run. It should create a durable run record, enqueue the work, and return immediately.

sentences.en: The first production pattern is to stop running the whole agent inside the web request.
sentences.zh: 第一个生产模式是停止在 Web 请求内运行整个代理。

sentences.en: A request is the wrong lifetime for an agent run.
sentences.zh: 请求对于代理运行来说是错误的生命周期。

sentences.en: It should create a durable run record, enqueue the work, and return immediately.
sentences.zh: 它应该创建持久的运行记录、将工作排队并立即返回。

blocks.html_en: That gives the application a simple boundary:

sentences.en: That gives the application a simple boundary:
sentences.zh: 这给了应用程序一个简单的边界：

blocks.html_en: The API enqueues the job. The queue stores the job durably. The worker executes the job. The database records progress.

sentences.en: The API enqueues the job.
sentences.zh: API 将作业排入队列。

sentences.en: The queue stores the job durably.
sentences.zh: 队列持久地存储作业。

sentences.en: The worker executes the job.
sentences.zh: 工人执行工作。

sentences.en: The database records progress.
sentences.zh: 数据库记录进度。

blocks.html_en: The client gets a run ID immediately. The agent runs somewhere else. The user checks status, subscribes to updates, or receives a callback when the run completes.

sentences.en: The client gets a run ID immediately.
sentences.zh: 客户端立即获得运行 ID。

sentences.en: The agent runs somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 代理运行在其他地方。

sentences.en: The user checks status, subscribes to updates, or receives a callback when the run completes.
sentences.zh: 用户检查状态、订阅更新或在运行完成时接收回调。

blocks.html_en: A queue is a durable buffer between the thing that creates work and the thing that performs it. This is the default starting point when runs are longer than a normal request, tasks are mostly independent, and you need worker scaling, retries, or burst absorption.

sentences.en: A queue is a durable buffer between the thing that creates work and the thing that performs it.
sentences.zh: 队列是创建工作的事物和执行工作的事物之间的持久缓冲区。

sentences.en: This is the default starting point when runs are longer than a normal request, tasks are mostly independent, and you need worker scaling, retries, or burst absorption.
sentences.zh: 当运行时间比正常请求长、任务大多是独立的并且您需要工作人员扩展、重试或突发吸收时，这是默认起点。

blocks.html_en: The trap: a queue knows a job exists, but it doesn't know the logical process that job belongs to. One background job is fine. Twenty dependent steps, three retries, two branches, and a human approval pause is not something a queue manages for you. You'll build that logic yourself. As we'll see later, that's where workflow engines come in.

sentences.en: The trap: a queue knows a job exists, but it doesn't know the logical process that job belongs to.
sentences.zh: 陷阱：队列知道作业存在，但不知道作业所属的逻辑进程。

sentences.en: One background job is fine.
sentences.zh: 一项后台工作就可以了。

sentences.en: Twenty dependent steps, three retries, two branches, and a human approval pause is not something a queue manages for you.
sentences.zh: 队列无法为您管理二十个相关步骤、三次重试、两个分支和人工批准暂停。

sentences.en: You'll build that logic yourself.
sentences.zh: 您将自己构建该逻辑。

sentences.en: As we'll see later, that's where workflow engines come in.
sentences.zh: 正如我们稍后将看到的，这就是工作流引擎的用武之地。

blocks.html_en: Reliability: safe retries and partial failure

sentences.en: Reliability: safe retries and partial failure
sentences.zh: 可靠性：安全重试和部分失败

blocks.html_en: Moving work to a queue solves the lifetime problem. It does not solve for durability of execution.

sentences.en: Moving work to a queue solves the lifetime problem.
sentences.zh: 将工作移至队列可以解决生命周期问题。

sentences.en: It does not solve for durability of execution.
sentences.zh: 它不能解决执行的持久性问题。

blocks.html_en: Most production queues are at-least-once: a job may run more than once. That's a deliberate tradeoff to avoid losing work, and your code has to survive it. Once an agent can call tools, write records, send messages, or provisions resources, retry behavior becomes part of the application’s correctness model.

sentences.en: Most production queues are at-least-once: a job may run more than once.
sentences.zh: 大多数生产队列至少运行一次：一个作业可能运行多次。

sentences.en: That's a deliberate tradeoff to avoid losing work, and your code has to survive it.
sentences.zh: 这是为了避免丢失工作而故意进行的权衡，并且您的代码必须能够幸存下来。

sentences.en: Once an agent can call tools, write records, send messages, or provisions resources, retry behavior becomes part of the application’s correctness model.
sentences.zh: 一旦代理可以调用​​工具、写入记录、发送消息或配置资源，重试行为就成为应用程序正确性模型的一部分。

blocks.html_en: Two disciplines matter most. Idempotency answers what happens when a single step runs twice. Compensation answers what happens when a run stops partway through a sequence of steps. Retries make the first a requirement. Permanent failures make the second necessary for production. Agents that touch remote services needs both.

sentences.en: Two disciplines matter most.
sentences.zh: 有两个学科最重要。

sentences.en: Idempotency answers what happens when a single step runs twice.
sentences.zh: 幂等性回答了单个步骤运行两次时会发生什么。

sentences.en: Compensation answers what happens when a run stops partway through a sequence of steps.
sentences.zh: 补偿解决了运行在一系列步骤中途停止时发生的情况。

sentences.en: Retries make the first a requirement.
sentences.zh: 重试使第一次成为一项要求。

sentences.en: Permanent failures make the second necessary for production.
sentences.zh: 永久性故障使得第二个故障成为生产所必需的。

sentences.en: Agents that touch remote services needs both.
sentences.zh: 接触远程服务的代理需要两者。

blocks.html_en: Bad worker code assumes no crash between steps:

sentences.en: Bad worker code assumes no crash between steps:
sentences.zh: 错误的工作代码假设步骤之间没有崩溃：

blocks.html_en: Better code creates an idempotency boundary:

sentences.en: Better code creates an idempotency boundary:
sentences.zh: 更好的代码创建幂等边界：

blocks.html_en: For agents, every side-effecting tool call needs the same treatment: check for a completed record before calling the tool, upsert a "running" record, call the tool, mark it complete.

sentences.en: For agents, every side-effecting tool call needs the same treatment: check for a completed record before calling the tool, upsert a "running" record, call the tool, mark it complete.
sentences.zh: 对于代理，每个副作用工具调用都需要相同的处理：在调用工具之前检查已完成的记录，更新插入“正在运行”的记录，调用该工具，将其标记为完成。

blocks.html_en: Retry is not a recovery strategy unless the retried operation is safe.

sentences.en: Retry is not a recovery strategy unless the retried operation is safe.
sentences.zh: 除非重试操作是安全的，否则重试不是恢复策略。

blocks.html_en: Consider an agent that completes three of five steps:

sentences.en: Consider an agent that completes three of five steps:
sentences.zh: 考虑一个代理完成五个步骤中的三个：

blocks.html_en: • it charges a card,

sentences.en: it charges a card,
sentences.zh: 它可以对卡进行收费，

blocks.html_en: • provisions a resource,

sentences.en: provisions a resource,
sentences.zh: 提供资源，

blocks.html_en: • and sends a confirmation email.

sentences.en: and sends a confirmation email.
sentences.zh: 并发送一封确认电子邮件。

blocks.html_en: Then step four then fails permanently. None of the first three steps can be rolled back with a database transaction, since a charge is not undone by deleting a database row; the money has already moved. Restarting the run from step one would recharge the card and resend the email, recreating the exact duplicate-side-effect problem idempotency was meant to prevent.

sentences.en: Then step four then fails permanently.
sentences.zh: 然后第四步就永久失败了。

sentences.en: None of the first three steps can be rolled back with a database transaction, since a charge is not undone by deleting a database row; the money has already moved.
sentences.zh: 前三个步骤都不能通过数据库事务回滚，因为删除数据库行无法撤消费用；钱已经转移了。

sentences.en: Restarting the run from step one would recharge the card and resend the email, recreating the exact duplicate-side-effect problem idempotency was meant to prevent.
sentences.zh: 从第一步重新开始运行将对卡进行充值并重新发送电子邮件，从而重新创建幂等性旨在防止的重复副作用问题。

blocks.html_en: Distributed systems have a standard answer to this: the saga pattern. For every side-effecting action an agent can take, define a compensating action that reverses the effect. A charge is reversed with a refund. An email is reversed with a correction message. When a run fails permanently, the orchestrator walks the completed steps in reverse order and runs their compensations.

sentences.en: Distributed systems have a standard answer to this: the saga pattern.
sentences.zh: 分布式系统对此有一个标准答案：传奇模式。

sentences.en: For every side-effecting action an agent can take, define a compensating action that reverses the effect.
sentences.zh: 对于代理可以采取的每个副作用操作，定义一个可逆转效果的补偿操作。

sentences.en: A charge is reversed with a refund.
sentences.zh: 费用被撤销并退款。

sentences.en: An email is reversed with a correction message.
sentences.zh: 电子邮件被撤销并附有更正消息。

sentences.en: When a run fails permanently, the orchestrator walks the completed steps in reverse order and runs their compensations.
sentences.zh: 当运行永久失败时，协调器会以相反的顺序执行已完成的步骤并运行其补偿。

blocks.html_en: Compensations must be idempotent in the same way forward actions are. Compensations can also fail on their own; a refund API can be unavailable just as easily as a charge API. A compensation chain needs a bounded retry, a dead-letter path for compensations that will not complete, and a manual escape hatch. Without these, a failed run can end up half-undone instead of half-done, which is not an improvement.

sentences.en: Compensations must be idempotent in the same way forward actions are.
sentences.zh: 补偿必须像前向行动一样是幂等的。

sentences.en: Compensations can also fail on their own; a refund API can be unavailable just as easily as a charge API.
sentences.zh: 补偿也可能自行失败；退款 API 可能与收费 API 一样容易不可用。

sentences.en: A compensation chain needs a bounded retry, a dead-letter path for compensations that will not complete, and a manual escape hatch.
sentences.zh: 补偿链需要有界重试、无法完成的补偿的死信路径以及手动逃生舱口。

sentences.en: Without these, a failed run can end up half-undone instead of half-done, which is not an improvement.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这些，失败的运行可能会导致一半未完成而不是完成一半，这并不是一种改进。

blocks.html_en: Compensation is not always the right response to a partial failure. If four of five parallel sub-orders succeeded and one failed, completing the four and dropping the fifth is often the better outcome. This avoids unwinding work that succeeded. Compensation is worth building when partial success is unacceptable, not as a default response to any failure.

sentences.en: Compensation is not always the right response to a partial failure.
sentences.zh: 补偿并不总是对部分故障的正确反应。

sentences.en: If four of five parallel sub-orders succeeded and one failed, completing the four and dropping the fifth is often the better outcome.
sentences.zh: 如果五个并行子订单中有四个成功而一个失败，则完成四个并放弃第五个通常是更好的结果。

sentences.en: This avoids unwinding work that succeeded.
sentences.zh: 这可以避免取消已成功的工作。

sentences.en: Compensation is worth building when partial success is unacceptable, not as a default response to any failure.
sentences.zh: 当部分成功不可接受时，值得建立补偿，而不是作为对任何失败的默认反应。

blocks.html_en: Idempotency covers a step that runs twice. Compensation covers a run that stops halfway through. Both are required whether the run is executed by a simple worker or by a workflow engine.

sentences.en: Idempotency covers a step that runs twice.
sentences.zh: 幂等性涵盖运行两次的步骤。

sentences.en: Compensation covers a run that stops halfway through.
sentences.zh: 补偿涵盖中途停止的跑步。

sentences.en: Both are required whether the run is executed by a simple worker or by a workflow engine.
sentences.zh: 无论运行是由简单工作线程执行还是由工作流引擎执行，两者都是必需的。

blocks.html_en: A queue distributes work, but it does not remember the shape of a run. It knows that a job exists. It does not know that step three depends on step two, that a human approval is pending, that two branches need to join before synthesis, or that compensation should run if the final step fails.

sentences.en: A queue distributes work, but it does not remember the shape of a run.
sentences.zh: 队列分配工作，但它不记住运行的形状。

sentences.en: It knows that a job exists.
sentences.zh: 它知道有一份工作存在。

sentences.en: It does not know that step three depends on step two, that a human approval is pending, that two branches need to join before synthesis, or that compensation should run if the final step fails.
sentences.zh: 它不知道第三步依赖于第二步，不知道人工批准正在等待，两个分支需要在综合之前加入，或者如果最后一步失败则应该运行补偿。

blocks.html_en: Once the hard part is no longer where should this job run? but what should happen next, given what already happened?, you have moved from queueing into orchestration.

sentences.en: Once the hard part is no longer where should this job run?
sentences.zh: 一旦困难部分不再存在，这项工作应该跑到哪里去呢？

sentences.en: but what should happen next, given what already happened?, you have moved from queueing into orchestration.
sentences.zh: 但是考虑到已经发生的事情，接下来会发生什么？您已经从排队转向编排。

blocks.html_en: A workflow engine provides that orchestration layer. It stores the history of a run: which steps started, completed, failed, retried, timed out, or waited for external input. In a workflow, a crash doesn't mean starting over.

sentences.en: A workflow engine provides that orchestration layer.
sentences.zh: 工作流引擎提供了该编排层。

sentences.en: It stores the history of a run: which steps started, completed, failed, retried, timed out, or waited for external input.
sentences.zh: 它存储运行的历史记录：哪些步骤开始、完成、失败、重试、超时或等待外部输入。

sentences.en: In a workflow, a crash doesn't mean starting over.
sentences.zh: 在工作流程中，崩溃并不意味着重新开始。

blocks.html_en: Every workflow system divides the code into the same two roles: a coordinator that decides what happens next, and steps that do the actual work — model calls, tool executions, record writes. The names vary from engine to engine, but the division of responsibility is the concept that matters: decisions live in one layer, effects live in the other.

sentences.en: Every workflow system divides the code into the same two roles: a coordinator that decides what happens next, and steps that do the actual work — model calls, tool executions, record writes.
sentences.zh: 每个工作流系统都将代码分为相同的两个角色：决定接下来发生什么的协调器，以及执行实际工作的步骤 - 模型调用、工具执行、记录写入。

sentences.en: The names vary from engine to engine, but the division of responsibility is the concept that matters: decisions live in one layer, effects live in the other.
sentences.zh: 不同引擎的名称各不相同，但责任划分是重要的概念：决策位于一层，效果位于另一层。

blocks.html_en: The coordinator has one hard rule: given the same history, it must always make the same decisions. This is because of how recovery works. After a crash, the engine rebuilds a run by re-executing the decision logic from the top, substituting recorded results for work that already completed. Replay only lands in the same place if the code decides the same way every time. So anything that could answer differently on a second pass — a model call, the current time, a random number, a call to an external service — belongs in a step, where the result is recorded the first time it runs and read back from history ever after. A stray clock read inside the coordinator, and a resumed run silently diverges from its own history. Durable execution tells you where a run was when it crashed. It does not remove the need for idempotency, because steps can still run more than once. This is why a workflow engine is the natural home for compensation logic: it already tracks which steps completed, which is the record a saga needs to walk backward.

sentences.en: The coordinator has one hard rule: given the same history, it must always make the same decisions.
sentences.zh: 协调器有一个硬性规则：鉴于相同的历史，它必须始终做出相同的决定。

sentences.en: This is because of how recovery works.
sentences.zh: 这是因为恢复的工作原理。

sentences.en: After a crash, the engine rebuilds a run by re-executing the decision logic from the top, substituting recorded results for work that already completed.
sentences.zh: 崩溃后，引擎通过从顶部重新执行决策逻辑来重建运行，用记录的结果替换已经完成的工作。

sentences.en: Replay only lands in the same place if the code decides the same way every time.
sentences.zh: 如果代码每次都以相同的方式决定，则重播只会落在同一位置。

sentences.en: So anything that could answer differently on a second pass — a model call, the current time, a random number, a call to an external service — belongs in a step, where the result is recorded the first time it runs and read back from history ever after.
sentences.zh: 因此，任何在第二遍时可能有不同答案的东西——模型调用、当前时间、随机数、对外部服务的调用——都属于一个步骤，在第一次运行时记录结果，并从以后的历史记录中读回。

sentences.en: A stray clock read inside the coordinator, and a resumed run silently diverges from its own history.
sentences.zh: 协调器内部的杂散时钟读取，并且恢复的运行默默地偏离了它自己的历史。

sentences.en: Durable execution tells you where a run was when it crashed.
sentences.zh: 持久执行会告诉您运行崩溃时的位置。

sentences.en: It does not remove the need for idempotency, because steps can still run more than once.
sentences.zh: 它并没有消除对幂等性的需求，因为步骤仍然可以运行多次。

sentences.en: This is why a workflow engine is the natural home for compensation logic: it already tracks which steps completed, which is the record a saga needs to walk backward.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么工作流引擎是补偿逻辑的天然家园：它已经跟踪完成了哪些步骤，这是传奇需要向后走的记录。

blocks.html_en: Scaling workflows: fan-out, fan-in, and contention

sentences.en: Scaling workflows: fan-out, fan-in, and contention
sentences.zh: 扩展工作流程：扇出、扇入和争用

blocks.html_en: Workflows become especially useful when a run branches. Fan-out is the common shape: a lead agent breaks a goal into independent subtasks, sends each to a worker or subagent, and then synthesizes the results.

sentences.en: Workflows become especially useful when a run branches.
sentences.zh: 当运行分支时，工作流变得特别有用。

sentences.en: Fan-out is the common shape: a lead agent breaks a goal into independent subtasks, sends each to a worker or subagent, and then synthesizes the results.
sentences.zh: 扇出是常见的形状：主导代理将目标分解为独立的子任务，将每个子任务发送给工作人员或子代理，然后综合结果。

blocks.html_en: This buys parallelism and fresh context windows, which is useful for research, document analysis, and other breadth-first work. But the hard part is not dispatching the workers. It is coordinating the fan-in: what happens if one branch fails, how many failures are tolerable, whether to synthesize partial results, and how to avoid waiting forever. A queue can run the workers. A workflow decides what happens next.

sentences.en: This buys parallelism and fresh context windows, which is useful for research, document analysis, and other breadth-first work.
sentences.zh: 这购买了并行性和新的上下文窗口，这对于研究、文档分析和其他广度优先工作很有用。

sentences.en: But the hard part is not dispatching the workers.
sentences.zh: 但困难的部分不是派遣工人。

sentences.en: It is coordinating the fan-in: what happens if one branch fails, how many failures are tolerable, whether to synthesize partial results, and how to avoid waiting forever.
sentences.zh: 它正在协调扇入：如果一个分支失败会发生什么，可以容忍多少次失败，是否合成部分结果，以及如何避免永远等待。

sentences.en: A queue can run the workers.
sentences.zh: 队列可以运行工作人员。

sentences.en: A workflow decides what happens next.
sentences.zh: 工作流程决定接下来会发生什么。

blocks.html_en: Fan-out is worth using when subtasks are independent, mostly read-only, and parallelizable. It works poorly when subtasks are tightly coupled or need to share state that keeps changing. Adding agents also adds cost and coordination overhead, so the question of how many agents to use matters more than the mechanics of spawning them.

sentences.en: Fan-out is worth using when subtasks are independent, mostly read-only, and parallelizable.
sentences.zh: 当子任务是独立的、大部分是只读的并且可并行时，扇出就值得使用。

sentences.en: It works poorly when subtasks are tightly coupled or need to share state that keeps changing.
sentences.zh: 当子任务紧密耦合或需要共享不断变化的状态时，它的工作效果很差。

sentences.en: Adding agents also adds cost and coordination overhead, so the question of how many agents to use matters more than the mechanics of spawning them.
sentences.zh: 添加代理还会增加成本和协调开销，因此使用多少代理的问题比生成代理的机制更重要。

blocks.html_en: Fan-out also introduces contention. A system can work with three parallel subagents and fail at eleven, even when there is plenty of aggregate provider capacity. Uncoordinated calls can collide on the same rate limit, exhaust the same connection pool, or retry at the same time. Treat providers, databases, and model APIs as shared resources: cap concurrency, use token buckets where needed, and back off when the shared resource pushes back.

sentences.en: Fan-out also introduces contention.
sentences.zh: 扇出也会引入争用。

sentences.en: A system can work with three parallel subagents and fail at eleven, even when there is plenty of aggregate provider capacity.
sentences.zh: 即使有足够的聚合提供商容量，系统也可以与三个并行子代理一起工作，并在十一个子代理时失败。

sentences.en: Uncoordinated calls can collide on the same rate limit, exhaust the same connection pool, or retry at the same time.
sentences.zh: 不协调的调用可能会在相同的速率限制上发生冲突、耗尽相同的连接池或同时重试。

sentences.en: Treat providers, databases, and model APIs as shared resources: cap concurrency, use token buckets where needed, and back off when the shared resource pushes back.
sentences.zh: 将提供程序、数据库和模型 API 视为共享资源：限制并发性、在需要时使用令牌桶，并在共享资源推迟时退出。

blocks.html_en: At scale, a workflow coordinates the process and a queue distributes execution. They are not competitors; they operate at different layers.

sentences.en: At scale, a workflow coordinates the process and a queue distributes execution.
sentences.zh: 在规模上，工作流协调流程，队列分配执行。

sentences.en: They are not competitors; they operate at different layers.
sentences.zh: 他们不是竞争对手；他们在不同的层面上运作。

blocks.html_en: Two details carry the weight here. Promise.allSettled keeps one failed branch from poisoning the entire fan-in, and the success threshold makes the partial-failure policy explicit: the workflow, not the queue, decides whether the run can proceed with what came back.

sentences.en: Two details carry the weight here.
sentences.zh: 这里有两个细节很重要。

sentences.en: Promise.allSettled keeps one failed branch from poisoning the entire fan-in, and the success threshold makes the partial-failure policy explicit: the workflow, not the queue, decides whether the run can proceed with what came back.
sentences.zh: Promise.allSettled 可以防止一个失败的分支对整个扇入造成影响，并且成功阈值使部分失败策略变得明确：工作流（而不是队列）决定运行是否可以继续执行返回的内容。

blocks.html_en: This is the mature pattern for high-scale agentic systems: durable process state, multiple worker pools, rate-limited dispatch, audibility. The cost is real operational complexity. You now have an API plane, an orchestration plane, and an execution plane. This is worth it when the workload demands it.

sentences.en: This is the mature pattern for high-scale agentic systems: durable process state, multiple worker pools, rate-limited dispatch, audibility.
sentences.zh: 这是大规模代理系统的成熟模式：持久的进程状态、多个工作池、限速调度、可听性。

sentences.en: The cost is real operational complexity.
sentences.zh: 成本是实际操作的复杂性。

sentences.en: You now have an API plane, an orchestration plane, and an execution plane.
sentences.zh: 您现在拥有一个 API 平面、一个编排平面和一个执行平面。

sentences.en: This is worth it when the workload demands it.
sentences.zh: 当工作负载需要时，这是值得的。

blocks.html_en: The patterns above are platform-agnostic. You can assemble them from any queue, any workflow engine, and any worker fleet. The question is how much of that assembly you want to own and operate.

sentences.en: The patterns above are platform-agnostic.
sentences.zh: 上述模式与平台无关。

sentences.en: You can assemble them from any queue, any workflow engine, and any worker fleet.
sentences.zh: 您可以从任何队列、任何工作流引擎和任何工作队列中组装它们。

sentences.en: The question is how much of that assembly you want to own and operate.
sentences.zh: 问题是您想拥有和运营该组件的多少部分。

blocks.html_en: On Render, the answer is almost none of it. Your web service is the API; Render Workflows is everything else. You define tasks as plain TypeScript or Python functions, and the platform provides the queue, the workers, the retries, the isolation, and per-run observability. There is no queue to provision, no worker fleet to keep warm, and no orchestrator cluster to operate.

sentences.en: On Render, the answer is almost none of it.

sentences.en: Your web service is the API; Render Workflows is everything else.

sentences.en: You define tasks as plain TypeScript or Python functions, and the platform provides the queue, the workers, the retries, the isolation, and per-run observability.
sentences.zh: 您将任务定义为普通的 TypeScript 或 Python 函数，平台提供队列、工作线程、重试、隔离和每次运行的可观察性。

sentences.en: There is no queue to provision, no worker fleet to keep warm, and no orchestrator cluster to operate.
sentences.zh: 没有需要配置的队列，没有需要保温的工作队列，也没有需要运行的协调器集群。

blocks.html_en: This is the entire execution plane. There is no queue client, no message schema, no polling loop, no worker registration. sentences.zh: 当runAgent调用decide(...)

Each pass through the loop decides again, given everything that has already happened — so actions can run in sequence across iterations, in parallel within one, and the run terminates when the model decides it is done (bounded by the task’s timeout).

sentences.en: The loop is the agent.

content_html_zh:
大多数团队开始构建代理的方式与构建任何其他 Web 功能相同：将模型包装在路由处理程序中，解析请求，然后等待响应。

这对于演示来说很好。 这也是生产中第一个中断的事情。

代理是长期运行的、有状态的且不确定的。 它们调用工具、等待外部 API、分支到子任务、达到速率限制，并在多步骤序列中途崩溃。 如果您的代理与单个 HTTP 请求相关联，则您已将应用程序的可靠性与非确定性循环的挂钟时间耦合起来。

超越演示意味着打破这种耦合。 这篇文章将介绍团队用来将脆弱的代理脚本转变为可扩展、有弹性的生产系统的三个核心模式。

代理的核心是一个循环：接收目标，决定下一步做什么，调用模型或工具，观察结果，更新状态，重复直到完成。 该循环有一些特性使其对朴素的 Web 架构产生敌意。

代理是长期运行的。 正常的 API 请求应该很快完成。 代理通常不会这样做，有时需要数小时甚至数天才能完成。

代理是有状态的。 一次运行不是一次函数调用。 它是一个目标、一个计划、工具调用和输出、重试、错误、决策和最终输出。 如果进程崩溃，您需要知道已经发生了什么。 如果没有，您要么会失去进度，要么盲目地重新运行工作。 两者都不是很好，特别是对于长期运行的代理来说。

代理是不确定的。 传统的工作流程代码是这样的：

代理代码说：

该模型在运行时选择下一个操作，这使得恢复、重放和调试变得更加困难。

跑步可能需要三步或三十步。 它可能会分散到多个工具上，等待人类，产生大量的中间工件，或者提前停止。 基础设施必须通过超时、预算、检查点、批准和明确的终止条件来围绕这种不可预测性设置边界。

总而言之，这些属性意味着代理需要的不仅仅是包装在应用程序代码中的模型调用。 他们需要将运行与请求分离的架构，以及保留进度、记录决策、控制副作用以及与模型上下文分开管理工件的基础设施。

第一个生产模式是停止在 Web 请求内运行整个代理。 请求对于代理运行来说是错误的生命周期。 它应该创建持久的运行记录、将工作排队并立即返回。

这给了应用程序一个简单的边界：

API 将作业排入队列。 队列持久地存储作业。 工人执行工作。 数据库记录进度。

客户端立即获得运行 ID。 代理运行在其他地方。 用户检查状态、订阅更新或在运行完成时接收回调。

队列是创建工作的事物和执行工作的事物之间的持久缓冲区。 当运行时间比正常请求长、任务大多是独立的并且您需要工作人员扩展、重试或突发吸收时，这是默认起点。

陷阱：队列知道作业存在，但不知道作业所属的逻辑进程。 一项后台工作就可以了。 队列无法为您管理二十个相关步骤、三次重试、两个分支和人工批准暂停。 您将自己构建该逻辑。 正如我们稍后将看到的，这就是工作流引擎的用武之地。

可靠性：安全重试和部分失败

将工作移至队列可以解决生命周期问题。 它不能解决执行的持久性问题。

大多数生产队列至少运行一次：一个作业可能运行多次。 这是为了避免丢失工作而故意进行的权衡，并且您的代码必须能够幸存下来。 一旦代理可以调用​​工具、写入记录、发送消息或配置资源，重试行为就成为应用程序正确性模型的一部分。

有两个学科最重要。 幂等性回答了单个步骤运行两次时会发生什么。 补偿解决了运行在一系列步骤中途停止时发生的情况。 重试使第一次成为一项要求。 永久性故障使得第二个故障成为生产所必需的。 接触远程服务的代理需要两者。

对于代理，每个副作用工具调用都需要相同的处理：在调用工具之前检查已完成的记录，更新插入“正在运行”的记录，调用该工具，将其标记为完成。

除非重试操作是安全的，否则重试不是恢复策略。

考虑一个代理完成五个步骤中的三个：

  1. 它可以对卡进行收费，
  2. 提供资源，
  3. 并发送一封确认电子邮件。

然后第四步就永久失败了。 前三个步骤都不能通过数据库事务回滚，因为删除数据库行无法撤消费用；钱已经转移了。 从第一步重新开始运行将对卡进行充值并重新发送电子邮件，从而重新创建幂等性旨在防止的重复副作用问题。

分布式系统对此有一个标准答案：传奇模式。 对于代理可以采取的每个副作用操作，定义一个可逆转效果的补偿操作。 费用被撤销并退款。 电子邮件被撤销并附有更正消息。 当运行永久失败时，协调器会以相反的顺序执行已完成的步骤并运行其补偿。

补偿必须像前向行动一样是幂等的。 补偿也可能自行失败；退款 API 可能与收费 API 一样容易不可用。 补偿链需要有界重试、无法完成的补偿的死信路径以及手动逃生舱口。 如果没有这些，失败的运行可能会导致一半未完成而不是完成一半，这并不是一种改进。

补偿并不总是对部分故障的正确反应。 如果五个并行子订单中有四个成功而一个失败，则完成四个并放弃第五个通常是更好的结果。 这可以避免取消已成功的工作。 当部分成功不可接受时，值得建立补偿，而不是作为对任何失败的默认反应。

幂等性涵盖运行两次的步骤。 补偿涵盖中途停止的跑步。 无论运行是由简单工作线程执行还是由工作流引擎执行，两者都是必需的。

队列分配工作，但它不记住运行的形状。 它知道有一份工作存在。 它不知道第三步依赖于第二步，不知道人工批准正在等待，两个分支需要在综合之前加入，或者如果最后一步失败则应该运行补偿。

一旦困难部分不再存在，这项工作应该跑到哪里去呢？ 但是考虑到已经发生的事情，接下来会发生什么？您已经从排队转向编排。

工作流引擎提供了该编排层。 它存储运行的历史记录：哪些步骤开始、完成、失败、重试、超时或等待外部输入。 在工作流程中，崩溃并不意味着重新开始。

每个工作流系统都将代码分为相同的两个角色：决定接下来发生什么的协调器，以及执行实际工作的步骤 - 模型调用、工具执行、记录写入。 不同引擎的名称各不相同，但责任划分是重要的概念：决策位于一层，效果位于另一层。

协调器有一个硬性规则：鉴于相同的历史，它必须始终做出相同的决定。 这是因为恢复的工作原理。 崩溃后，引擎通过从顶部重新执行决策逻辑来重建运行，用记录的结果替换已经完成的工作。 如果代码每次都以相同的方式决定，则重播只会落在同一位置。 因此，任何在第二遍时可能有不同答案的东西——模型调用、当前时间、随机数、对外部服务的调用——都属于一个步骤，在第一次运行时记录结果，并从以后的历史记录中读回。 协调器内部的杂散时钟读取，并且恢复的运行默默地偏离了它自己的历史。 持久执行会告诉您运行崩溃时的位置。 它并没有消除对幂等性的需求，因为步骤仍然可以运行多次。 这就是为什么工作流引擎是补偿逻辑的天然家园：它已经跟踪完成了哪些步骤，这是传奇需要向后走的记录。

扩展工作流程：扇出、扇入和争用

当运行分支时，工作流变得特别有用。 扇出是常见的形状：主导代理将目标分解为独立的子任务，将每个子任务发送给工作人员或子代理，然后综合结果。

这购买了并行性和新的上下文窗口，这对于研究、文档分析和其他广度优先工作很有用。 但困难的部分不是派遣工人。 它正在协调扇入：如果一个分支失败会发生什么，可以容忍多少次失败，是否合成部分结果，以及如何避免永远等待。 队列可以运行工作人员。 工作流程决定接下来会发生什么。

当子任务是独立的、大部分是只读的并且可并行时，扇出就值得使用。 当子任务紧密耦合或需要共享不断变化的状态时，它的工作效果很差。 添加代理还会增加成本和协调开销，因此使用多少代理的问题比生成代理的机制更重要。

扇出也会引入争用。 即使有足够的聚合提供商容量，系统也可以与三个并行子代理一起工作，并在十一个子代理时失败。 不协调的调用可能会在相同的速率限制上发生冲突、耗尽相同的连接池或同时重试。 将提供程序、数据库和模型 API 视为共享资源：限制并发性、在需要时使用令牌桶，并在共享资源推迟时退出。

在规模上，工作流协调流程，队列分配执行。 他们不是竞争对手；他们在不同的层面上运作。

这里有两个细节很重要。 Promise.allSettled 可以防止一个失败的分支对整个扇入造成影响，并且成功阈值使部分失败策略变得明确：工作流（而不是队列）决定运行是否可以继续执行返回的内容。

这是大规模代理系统的成熟模式：持久的进程状态、多个工作池、限速调度、可听性。 成本是实际操作的复杂性。 您现在拥有一个 API 平面、一个编排平面和一个执行平面。 当工作负载需要时，这是值得的。

上述模式与平台无关。 您可以从任何队列、任何工作流引擎和任何工作队列中组装它们。 问题是您想拥有和运营该组件的多少部分。

在渲染方面，答案几乎是否定的。 您的 Web 服务就是 API；渲染工作流程就是其他一切。 您将任务定义为普通的 TypeScript 或 Python 函数，平台提供队列、工作线程、重试、隔离和每次运行的可观察性。 没有需要配置的队列，没有需要保温的工作队列，也没有需要运行的协调器集群。

这是整个执行平面。 没有队列客户端，没有消息模式，没有轮询循环，没有工作人员注册。 三个 task() 包装器替换了第一个模式中的 API → Queue → Worker 管道。 当runAgent调用decide(...) 或executeAction(...)，这不是本地函数调用——因为函数被包装在task()中，每个调用都会启动一个在其自己的按需实例上运行的链式任务，具有自己的重试策略和自己的计算配置文件。 Promise.all 是扇出；该平台处理调度、隔离和重试。

循环是代理。 协调员不执行固定计划。 考虑到已经发生的所有事情，每次循环都会再次做出决定 - 因此操作可以在迭代中按顺序运行，在一次迭代中并行运行，并且当模型决定完成时运行终止（受任务超时限制）。

一次代理运行是一棵任务运行树。 runAgent的运行是根；每个decide 和executeAction 运行都与它相关联。 渲染跟踪整个树——状态、重试、每次运行的日志——所以“代理做了什么？” 这是仪表板可以回答的问题。 如果您的应用程序需要自己的记录，请存储根运行的 ID 并从那里开始。

从您的 Web 服务或其他任何地方启动代理运行是一个 SDK 调用：

startTask 是入队。 该平台持久地存储工作、调度它并公开其状态——在一次调用中从第一个模式开始的整个边界。 （如果调用者想要阻塞直到完成，则 runTask 会这样做；对于 API 请求边界，startTask 是合适的选择。）

工作流程是重心，但当运行需要更多时，平台的其余部分就会发挥作用。 调用 startTask 的 Cron Job 为您提供预定的代理。 当并行运行竞争共享速率限制时，键值会为您提供令牌桶。 Postgres 拥有大量工件，因此任务会传递 ID 而不是有效负载 - 状态必须比运行时保存在存储中；状态不得在运行之间与容器一起泄漏。 这些都不是开始所必需的；每个都是一个原语，在工作负载需要时添加。

工作流程消除了队列和工作人员管道。 如今，它并没有消除应用程序级别的正确性工作：幂等性、补偿、工件存储、跟踪传播、审批边界、成本控制和速率限制仍然由您使用本文中的模式来构建。

不过，这个界限正在移动。 此列表中的大部分内容正是工作流的发展方向：更强的持久性保证、一流的幂等性以及诸如本机审批门之类的人机交互原语都在路线图上。 本文中的模式将保持不变，但预计更多的模式将作为平台功能而不是您维护的应用程序代码提供。

工作流程现已处于 Beta 阶段，目前在支持的语言、调度、蓝图支持和 HIPAA 兼容主机方面存在限制。

任何平台都无法消除编排的设计负担。 您仍然必须决定状态所在的位置、重试的安全位置、批准的位置以及如何端到端跟踪运行。 该平台的工作是让这些决策的实施成本低廉，而不是为您做出决策。

下一代代理应用程序将像分布式系统一样构建，无论底层基础设施是手动的还是托管的。

请记住，队列会询问：这项工作应该在哪里运行？ 工作流程会问：考虑到已经发生的事情，接下来应该发生什么？ 代理人问：接下来我应该做什么来实现目标？

渲染工作流程可以使执行层更简单。 它可以启动任务运行、对它们进行排队、重试并显示它们的状态。 但应用程序仍然拥有运行的语义：什么算作进度，哪些副作用可以安全地重试，工件位于何处，何时必须由人类批准，以及如何修复部分故障。

那才是真正的境界。 基础设施带动工作。 工作流程保持进度。 代理选择操作。 可靠的代理应用程序来自于将这些职责分开，即使平台使它们易于一起部署。

渲染工作流程处于测试阶段。 如果您想运行这些模式而不构建其背后的基础设施，请从工作流文档开始。
